claims.text: 147 US institutions ever filed a polymer program in the federal record, 1991–2023, across 33 states, the District of Columbia and Puerto Rico, which is the 35 jurisdictions the hero card counts. This claim's prose read '35 states plus Puerto Rico' until 2026-08-31, which adds to 36 and drops the District of Columbia; the page itself has always printed the split correctly, and the assertion now pins the 33 as well as the 35. 41 institutions had a program still conferring in 2023. 'Ever' is a 33-year union and 'still conferring' a one-year snapshot — different constructs, never stated as a ratio. Added 2026-09-01: the record holds 20,052 lifetime completions and no institution's last conferring year is 2020. Both are pinned here because until that date it held 20,859 and four institutions read 2020 — the federal mirror's duplicated year, quarantined on 2026-08-26 for every other page built on that mirror and left inside this one, which was then promoted to the public tree with it. The three counts above are the ones that survived the duplicate untouched, and their surviving is exactly why nothing here caught the ones that did not.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, aggregated to institutions, source='ipeds' only, with 2020 quarantined
claims.assert: D['totals']['ever'] == 147 and D['totals']['active'] == 41 and D['totals']['states'] == 35 and len([x for x in D['states_list'] if x['state'] not in ('DC', 'PR')]) == 33 and len(D['states_list']) == 35 and len(D['dots']) == 146 and len(D['off_projection']) == 1 and D['off_projection'][0]['unitid'] == 242617 and D['totals']['active'] == sum(1 for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection'] if d['active_programs'] > 0) and sum(d['total_awards'] for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection']) == 20052 and not [d for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection'] if d['last_year'] == 2020] and D['quarantined'] == {'2020': 'the Urban Institute IPEDS mirror serves 2019 data under year=2020'}
claims.falsified_if: 2024 data lands or IPEDS revises (the census probes every build); or the mixed-denominator trap re-enters — any sentence stating 41-of-147 as a survival rate fails the census's own documented kill of that headline. Or Urban reloads completions-cip-6 and 2020 stops being a copy of 2019, at which point the year is real, the quarantine lifts, and this page is rebuilt rather than patched.

claims.text: Every one of the 147 institutions is placed: 146 on the map, one (Inter American University of Puerto Rico–San Germán) named beside it because AlbersUSA carries no Puerto Rico inset. Seven institutions that left the directory before 2009 sit at their city's centroid, and each says so in its hover. They are placed by hand because no directory vintage carries a coordinate for them, which is a fact about the directory and not about the institutions: two of the seven are still operating today. `totals.mapped` is 147 and counts GEOCODING, not drawing: every institution got a coordinate from the IPEDS directory, which is why `totals.unmapped` is 0, and the map draws 146 of them because one falls outside the frame, which is why `totals.dropped_outside_projection` is 1. The opening strip draws all 147, because it places an institution by the size of its record and a size axis has no projection to fall off.
claims.source: IPEDS directory coordinates via the Urban Institute API, with per-dot provenance
claims.assert: D['totals']['unmapped'] == 0 and len(D['dots']) + len(D['off_projection']) == D['totals']['ever'] == D['totals']['mapped'] == 147 and D['totals']['dropped_outside_projection'] == len(D['off_projection']) == 1 and len(D['dots']) == D['totals']['mapped'] - D['totals']['dropped_outside_projection'] and sum(1 for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection'] if d['coord_source'].startswith('hand')) == 7 and all('coord_source' in d for d in D['dots']) and all(k in D['off_projection'][0] for k in ('total_awards', 'active_programs'))
claims.actual: (D['totals'], sorted(set(d['coord_source'] for d in D['dots'] if d['coord_source'].startswith('hand'))))
claims.falsified_if: A directory vintage supplies real coordinates for one of the seven centroids (prefer it and drop the hand row), or a new census institution fails every directory year and the unmapped count leaves zero — at which point the page must grow a 'not mapped' table, not a guess. Added 2026-09-01: `mapped` and the drawn count are now pinned to each other. They stood at 147 against 146 with nothing asserting the difference, which reads as drift rather than as two names for two different things, and the opening strip had taken the wrong one of them into a hand-typed caption of 147 over 146 ticks. If a future projection gains a Puerto Rico inset, `dropped_outside_projection` goes to 0, `off_projection` empties, and this claim is restated rather than quietly re-counted.

claims.text: The deepest institutional teaching record is UMass Lowell's: 2,830 lifetime completions across its polymer programs, still conferring. This claim asserted 2,929 from 2026-08-21 until 2026-09-01 and was green every day of it: the census beneath it counted the federal mirror's duplicated 2020, which is 2019 served a second time, and 99 of Lowell's completions were that duplicate. A claim can only be as true as the data it is checked against, which is the whole reason verify_series.py is a separate gate from this one.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db census, institution-level sum, with the quarantined 2020 removed (_data/build/atlas_reprojection_patch.py)
claims.assert: 'Massachusetts-Lowell' in D['top']['name'] and D['top']['total_awards'] == 2830 and D['top']['total_awards'] == max(d['total_awards'] for d in D['dots']) and (lambda t: t['active_programs'] > 0)(one(d for d in D['dots'] if d['unitid'] == D['top']['unitid']))
claims.falsified_if: A revision or the 2024 vintage reorders the top — Ferris State's record is second and Akron's third, and shrinking annual output means those gaps now only widen, so a change here would signal a data problem before a real one. The line read "Akron's record is second" until 2026-09-01; Akron has been third since the page was built, and nothing asserted the order, so the sentence was never checked by anything.

claims.text: Standfirst and the third band's headline: the three deepest records are the University of Massachusetts Lowell, Ferris State University in Big Rapids, Michigan, and the University of Akron, and between them they hold more than a third of every degree and certificate in the record.
claims.assert: (lambda t, A: [d['city'] for d in t] == ['Lowell', 'Big Rapids', 'Akron'] and 'Massachusetts-Lowell' in t[0]['name'] and 'Ferris State' in t[1]['name'] and 'Akron' in t[2]['name'] and sum(d['total_awards'] for d in t) * 3 > A and sum(d['total_awards'] for d in t) * 2 < A)(sorted((D['dots'] + D['off_projection']), key=lambda d: -d['total_awards'])[:3], sum(d['total_awards'] for d in (D['dots'] + D['off_projection'])))
claims.actual: ([(d['name'], d['city'], d['total_awards']) for d in sorted((D['dots'] + D['off_projection']), key=lambda d: -d['total_awards'])[:3]], sum(d['total_awards'] for d in (D['dots'] + D['off_projection'])))
claims.falsified_if: A restated year changes the order of the top three, moves any of them out of Lowell, Big Rapids or Akron, or takes their combined share below a third. The upper bound is asserted too: if the three ever passed half the record, 'more than a third' would be understating it and the standfirst would have to be rewritten rather than left technically true.

claims.text: At institution level Michigan leads with 15 institutions ever to Ohio's 14 — while the programs page shows Ohio first on substantive programs. Institutions and programs are different units; both rankings are true and the page says so rather than picking the flattering one.
claims.assert: D['states_list'][0]['state'] == 'MI' and D['states_list'][0]['ever'] == 15 and D['states_list'][1]['state'] == 'OH' and D['states_list'][1]['ever'] == 14
claims.falsified_if: A revision flips the order — at a one-institution margin, a single recoded campus does it. If Ohio takes the institution lead too, the construct lesson stays and the sentence flips.

claims.text: Four institutions confirmed to teach polymer science under chemistry or chemical-engineering codes — UChicago (Pritzker), Dartmouth, Rutgers and Brown — are drawn as hollow diamonds: the census's blind spot made visible on the map itself. There are certainly more; these are the verified ones.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db README, 'confirmed cases' — each verified against the institution's own program pages during the census build
claims.checked_by: Claude (2026-08-21 build), against the census's confirmed-cases list; the four were verified during the census build, not re-verified today
claims.falsified_if: Any of the four starts filing under a polymer CIP (it then becomes a dot and leaves this list), or a fifth institution is confirmed (add it — the list understates by design and growing it strengthens the point).

claims.text: The research layer — institution-level polymer output from OpenAlex subfield 2507 — is deliberately absent from this version: its candidate list is zero-verified and the API is metered. It is the named next step, not a silent omission.
claims.source: polymer-programs-db known_gaps.md (openalex_candidates.tsv, 'zero individually verified'); the API-REGISTRY OpenAlex row (metered, daily budget)
claims.falsified_if: The candidates get verified and fetched under budget — at which point this claim is retired and the layer ships with its own claims.

claims.text: The pale marks on this page mean one thing and the page says only that thing: the institution filed no completion under any of the three polymer CIP codes in the single year 2023. 106 of the 147 rows are pale on that test. The word 'ended' is gone from the key, the legend, the hover, the screen-reader text and both table headers, because it was read as 'closed' and that is false for most of the 106. Four pale rows were checked against the institutions' own live catalogues on 2026-09-01 and all four are still teaching the subject: Northwest State Community College (plastics AAS and certificate), Mid Michigan College (AIM Plastics AAS), Davis Technical College (composites) and Skagit Valley College (composites inside an advanced-manufacturing AAS). Of the seven institutions the directory lost before 2009, three rows are confirmed closures (Akron Machining Institute 2007; Acme Institute of Technology's two Wisconsin campuses 1995, two rows for one school), two are operating (Westlawn Institute of Marine Technology; the Red Wing campus of Minnesota State College Southeast), and two are unestablished. The atlas therefore states three confirmed closures out of seven, never seven.
claims.source: the flag is polymer-programs-db active_programs; the operating statuses are documentary: westlawn.edu and Bangor Daily News 2010-07-20; southeastmn.edu institutional history and the 2024 Red Wing renovation; Wisconsin DSPS closed-schools register (Acme, 1995); IPEDS inst_status=4 with a 07/2007 close date (Akron Machining Institute); MSCHE reaffirmation 2025-06-06 (Inter American, San German); institutional catalogues for the four still-teaching cases
claims.assert: (lambda A: sum(1 for d in A if d['active_programs'] == 0) == 106 and sum(1 for d in A if d['active_programs'] > 0) == 41 and len(A) == 147 and set(d['unitid'] for d in A if d['coord_source'].startswith('hand'))     == {200794, 143899, 381848, 130703, 174659, 238139, 238148} and all(one(x for x in A if x['unitid'] == u)['active_programs'] == 0         for u in (200794, 143899, 381848, 130703, 174659, 238139, 238148)) and all(one(x for x in A if x['unitid'] == u)['active_programs'] == 0         for u in (204440, 171155, 230162, 236638, 172644)) and one(x for x in A if x['unitid'] == 242617)['last_year'] == 1999)(D['dots'] + D['off_projection'])
claims.actual: (sum(1 for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection'] if d['active_programs'] == 0), sorted(d['unitid'] for d in D['dots'] + D['off_projection']        if d['coord_source'].startswith('hand')))
claims.checked_by: Claude (2026-09-01), documentary check of the seven pre-2009 rows and of five pale rows against live institutional catalogues; the flag itself is machine-checked above
claims.falsified_if: Any of the seven pre-2009 rows is shown to have closed after all (move it from 'unestablished' to 'confirmed', and raise the three), or one of the two named operating institutions is shown to have closed (the sentence naming it must go), or a later IPEDS vintage moves a row off the 106. The count of confirmed closures may only change with a dated source attached. If any page word for the pale marks reverts to 'ended', 'closed', 'defunct' or 'gone', this claim is broken whatever the data says.

claims.text: The 147 counts IPEDS unitids, not distinct institutions, and three pairs of rows are one institution each: Penn State (495767 retired, 214777 current), New York University (194541 Polytechnic, 193900), and Acme Institute of Technology's two Wisconsin campuses (238139, 238148). All six rows carry no polymer-coded award in 2023, so collapsing them would take the distinct-institution count to about 144 and the pale count to about 103. The page prints 147 and 106 because every figure on it is built from rows, and it discloses the overcount in the methodology rather than silently recounting: the collapse is a data change, and it is the named next step.
claims.source: atlas/data/viz-data.json unitids, against the IPEDS unitid retirement history
claims.assert: (lambda A: len(A) == 147 and all(one(x for x in A if x['unitid'] == u)['active_programs'] == 0         for u in (495767, 214777, 194541, 193900, 238139, 238148)) and len(A) - 3 == 144 and sum(1 for d in A if d['active_programs'] == 0) - 3 == 103)(D['dots'] + D['off_projection'])
claims.actual: [(x['unitid'], x['name'], x['active_programs']) for x in D['dots'] + D['off_projection'] if x['unitid'] in (495767, 214777, 194541, 193900, 238139, 238148)]
claims.falsified_if: The build collapses the pairs (then 147 and 106 must fall to 144 and 103 everywhere on the page and in every claim here, and this claim is retired), or a fourth duplicate pair is found (raise the arithmetic and keep the disclosure), or one of the six rows starts conferring again, which would change the pale count without changing the distinct count.
